name: KS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -16 point partisan lean
Incumbent Tracey Mann running with a large financial advantage ($2.7M cash on hand vs. $4.8K)
Prediction markets price the Republican at 94%
Minimal Democratic fundraising and no outside spending signals
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Mann's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing a Republican win at 94% all point to a safe Republican hold. The Democratic challenger's negligible fundraising gives no basis to move the forecast.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major redistricting change affecting the district's boundaries could alter the picture.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kansas's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent Tracey Mann is seeking another term with every structural advantage. He has raised nearly $1.5 million and holds $2.7 million on hand, while Democrat Lauren Reinhold has raised under $50,000 with minimal cash remaining. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but lacks any visible campaign infrastructure.

Prediction markets give Mann roughly a 94% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's sixteen-point Republican lean, Mann's incumbency bonus, and the lopsided money advantage. Barring an unforeseen development, Mann is positioned for a comfortable re-election.
